p:cNvPr.descr: The process of converting beta-carotene and vitamin A into various retinoids, whose individual structures are shown. (a) Beta-carotene (labeled below). The beta-carotene consists of a closed 6-sided ring structure with one double bond on its bottom left. It has two single bonds off one carbon at the top right, and one single bond off the left side of the ring. A dashed pink line bisects the ring vertically. From the top of the ring is an 18-carbon chain, in the standard zigzag formation. Every other bond in the chain is a double bond. Four single bonds come in alternating directions at various points along the chain, going up. There are 4 dashed pink lines crossing 4 of the double bonds on the chain. On the ninth bond in the chain (a double bond) there is an arrow labeled "point of cleavage," showing where the chain is broken. The chain bonds to another 6-sided ring structure with one double bond, and a diagonal pink dashed line bisects the ring. The ring has 2 single bonds coming right off a single carbon in the ring, and one single bond on the lower right side of the ring. To the right is an arrow pointing to (b) all-trans-retinal (labeled below). Trans-retinal consists of the top six-carbon ring bonded down to half of the aforementioned chain, which is hanging down. The carbons on the trans-retinal are numbered. C2 is on the right side of the circle. The double bond is on C6-C7. Carbons 11 and 12 are also numbered futher down. There are still alternating double bonds for a total of 4 in the chain. C15, at the bottom of the chain, bonds left to H and double bonds right to O. This aldehyde is shaded orange. There is a right arrow with text above reading, "oxidation of aldehyde to acid." (c) All-trans-retinoic acid (labeled below). The previously described chain now has C15 bonded left to OH, double bonded right to H. This area is shaded orange. From (b), all-trans-retinal, there is a down equilibrium arrow, pointing to (d) all-trans-retinol (Vitamin A1)(labeled below). Here, the slanted double bond between C11 and C12 is shaded blue. The group on C15 is now CH2OH, shaded orange. A right arrow has text above it reading, "oxidation of alcohol to aldehyde." (e) 11-cis-retinal (visual pigment of rhodopsin) is the next molecule. Now, the double bond between C11 and C12 in the chain has been straightened, so that is no longer part of the zigzag. The bonds between C10 and C11, and C12 and C13, also no longer zigzag but rather plateau up to the double bond between C11 and C12 (shaded blue), so that the molecule is now cis. The bottom group is now C15 bonded left to H and double bonded right to O, now an aldehyde once more. A right arrow is to the right of this molecule, with a wavy right arrow above it. Text above the arrow reads, "visible light." (e) The all-trans-retinal (labeled below) is now back to its trans configuration, with the double bond between C11 and C12 (shaded blue) now in the trans formation and part of the zigzag carbon chain. C15 still bonds left to H and double bonds right to O and is shaded orange. A right arrow points to a gray box with text inside reading, "Neuronal signal (vision)."
